name: Vladimir Lenin
role: Revolutionary and Soviet head of government
description: Bolshevik revolutionary whose government established one-party rule and a predominantly state-directed economy.
scope: Public positions and conduct during the specified period; this represents the individual rather than all party members or citizens.

axes.brief: Bolshevik authority displaced the Constituent Assembly and excluded rival parties.
axes.counter: Workers’ councils and revolutionary participation were not equal competitive multiparty elections.

axes.brief: The Cheka, censorship and coercion defended revolutionary authority.
axes.counter: Pre-revolutionary opposition to tsarist repression differs from post-revolutionary governing practice.

axes.brief: National self-determination and minority languages challenged imperial assimilation.
axes.counter: Central party power and revolutionary political conformity qualified cultural autonomy.

axes.brief: International worker solidarity and revolutionary asylum supply comparatively open context.
axes.counter: Security and wartime controls complicate ordinary immigration analogies.

axes.brief: Civil war and revolutionary military organisation involved substantial force.
axes.counter: Brest-Litovsk accepted costly concessions to end war and preserve the revolution.

axes.brief: Revolutionary internationalism coexisted with state and party sovereignty.
axes.counter: International class solidarity does not prove acceptance of contemporary interstate courts.

axes.brief: Major industry and banking were nationalised.
axes.counter: The New Economic Policy restored limited private production and trade.

reasons.0: Major industrial and banking ownership remained public, but NEP private shops and small production weaken the claim that every ordinary business should reject private ownership.

axes.brief: A state foreign-trade monopoly and national economic control limited independent trade.
axes.counter: Pragmatic foreign deals and NEP were substantial exceptions to autarky.

axes.brief: Central direction and controls predominated while NEP restored market mechanisms.
axes.counter: Period variation is substantial; small producers and trade were not uniformly directed after 1921.

axes.brief: Land redistribution and elimination of class privilege pursued material equality.
axes.counter: Confiscation differed from the compensated land transfers in the question.

reasons.14: Revolutionary land transfer fits the first clause, but compensation of former large owners conflicts with confiscatory practice. A mixed response to the combined proposition is more likely than unqualified agreement.

axes.brief: Secular socialist civil authority excluded clerical power.
axes.counter: Anti-religious repression is not synonymous with liberal religious freedom.

axes.brief: Civil divorce, reproductive reform and women’s participation broke with older institutions.
axes.counter: Modern gender identity and same-sex marriage were not established policy endorsements.

axes.brief: Electrification and technical modernisation were revolutionary priorities.
axes.counter: Contemporary biomedical risk questions remain low-confidence translations.

axes.brief: National self-determination coexisted with tightly centralised party authority.
axes.counter: Formal federal rights and opposition to Stalin’s national chauvinism qualify centralism.

axes.brief: Class relationships, education and social transformation explained political behaviour.
axes.counter: Historical materialism does not answer every modern psychological genetics comparison.
